_what: Source of truth for the three tiny AI examples (SPEC.md, Functional specification). train.py fits parameters to these label rules; golden.py and the RTL implement the widths and the stream behaviour below.

stream.input: one item per beat in s_data[7:0]; s_last marks the final beat of a frame
stream.output: two beats: beat 0 = {6'b0, error, class}, beat 1 = score (8-bit, two's complement), m_last on beat 1
stream.error: a beat whose s_data exceeds input_max (the beat is not used), or a frame whose length is not exactly inputs; beats past inputs are ignored
stream.latency: clock edges from the edge that accepts the last input beat to the edge that raises m_valid, counting both

vision_all_lit.label: 1 when all four pixels are 1
vision_all_lit.model: one binary neuron: score = count of pixels equal to their 1-bit weight; class = score >= threshold

vision_block.label: 1 when some 2x2 window of the 3x3 image is fully lit
vision_block.model: one 2x2 binary kernel neuron reused serially at the four positions (one per cycle), OR max-pooling; window bit order TL, TR, BL, BR
vision_block.score: unsigned 0..4, the largest window match count

text_sentiment.label: 1 when the number of GOOD tokens is greater than the number of BAD tokens
text_sentiment.model: signed embedding lookup per token, four-term sum; class = sum > 0 (a sum of 0 is negative)
text_sentiment.score: signed sum, -16..12 by width, sign-extended to 8 bits
